**Status, stated before the mathematics.**

- **The merge inequality proves far more than it has been asked for, and the
  extra is two LATTICE laws.** For an optimal partition `P`, merging *any* set
  `S` of parts is a competitor, so **`5 e_Q(S) ≤ 6(|S|−1)` for EVERY `S`** —
  the quotient multigraph `Q` on the parts is **simple** (`|S| = 2`) and has
  **girth `≥ 6`** (`|S| = 3, 4, 5` forbid a triangle, a 4-cycle and a 5-cycle),
  with a 6-cycle allowed but **TIGHT**. And the partition weight
  `g(P) = 5 e_in(P) + 6|P| − 6n` is **supermodular** on the partition lattice,
  so the **join of two optimal partitions is optimal**: there is a unique
  **coarsest** optimal partition `P_max`, and **`δ_uv = 0 ⟺ u, v` lie in one
  block of `P_max`** — which makes *"`δ = 0`"* an **EQUIVALENCE RELATION**.
  **(BE-39)(i)/(ii)**.
- **Hence the SHORT-CYCLE LAW, and it is the theorem (BE-32)(ii)/(iii) were
  two instances of.** The crossing edges of a cycle `C` form a closed walk in
  `Q` with **distinct** edges, hence an even subgraph, hence contain a
  `Q`-cycle of length `≥ 6`. So the number of crossings is `0` or `≥ 6`:
  **every cycle of length `≤ 5` lies inside a single part of every optimal
  partition**, and a 6-cycle either does or splits into **six** parts forming a
  **tight** set whose merge is again optimal. Either way
  **`δ_xy = 0` for any `x, y` on a common cycle of length `≤ 6`**, and in
  general **`δ_xy ≤ max(0, L − 6)`** on a common `L`-cycle — which beats
  (BE-32)(iv)'s `δ ≤ dist` for every `L ≤ 11`. **(BE-32)(ii) is `L = 3`;
  (BE-32)(iii) is `L = 4` and its hypothesis WEAKENS from `≥ 3` common
  neighbours to `≥ 2`.** **(BE-40)**.
- **(BE-32)(+) is thereby PROVED at 196 043 of 203 723 aggressively-forced
  pairs, and REDUCED to a statement with no geometry in it.** Every forcing
  step whose three points put **two in one closed star** puts the admitted hub
  on a triangle or a 4-cycle with that star's centre — **401 489 of 401 544
  steps**, and the **first** step is *always* of that shape, which is exactly
  why (BE-32)(ii)/(iii) are the base case. What is left is *"every
  aggressively-forced pair is `≤6`-cycle-class connected"* — **measured at
  203 723 pairs with zero escapes**, and the residue is the **SPREAD** step, at
  **55** of 401 544. **(BE-41)**.
- **The proof's boundary is LOCATED, and it is exactly where the merge
  inequality runs out of slack.** A 6-cycle of `Q` is tight and a 7-cycle is
  not (`5·7 = 35 < 36`), so (BE-40) cannot reach past 6 — and a **named
  triangle-chain family** produces forcing steps whose shortest cycle is
  `7, 8, …`, escaping the certificate. **`δ = 0` at every member anyway**, and
  a blind hunt in the non-vacuous band (`def₃ > 0`) over **27 414** forced
  pairs finds **zero** escapes and **zero** `δ ≠ 0`. **(BE-41)(iii)**.
- **(b2) IS A COROLLARY OF (b1), by one line of Grassmann — job 2's clause
  stops being independent.** `Π_u ⊆ Z`, so for any subspace `X`
  **`dim(X ∩ Z) ≤ dim Z − 2 + dim(X ∩ Π_u)`**, and the same at `v`. Hence
  **(b1) ⟹ (b2) outright whenever `δ₁ ≥ 5`**, and `ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u = 0` at **either**
  end gives (b2) at **every** `δ₁`. The only pieces needing more are those with
  `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u) ≥ 1` at **both** ends and `δ₁ ≤ 4` — the **series** shape at
  both ends, where (BE-38)(i) settles the all-S piece and the SPQR peel is the
  stated route for the rest. Measured on bearcase's free sampler
  **extended to `dist_{G₁}(u,v) ≥ 5`**, which is precisely what (BE-38)(ii)'s
  transfer does not reach: **19 pieces, 0 failures**, the bound holding as an
  exact inequality at every draw and **tight at 144** of them. **(BE-42)**.
- **THE ROUTING VERDICT IS *NO*, and it is a theorem rather than a
  preference.** In a **chord-free** open ear decomposition the **last** ear has
  length `≥ 2` and receives no later attachment, so its interior vertices have
  degree **exactly 2** in `G`; if there is no ear at all, `G` is a cycle. So
  **`G` chord-free-ear-decomposable ⟹ `G` has a degree-2 vertex** —
  contrapositively **every graph of minimum degree `≥ 3`, i.e. every 3-connected
  block, i.e. every R-NODE, forces a single-edge ear in EVERY open ear
  decomposition.** Swept: **2 084 3-connected graphs, ZERO chord-free**;
  6 968 of 12 620 2-connected graphs chord-free, **every one** of them with a
  degree-2 vertex. And the single-edge step is **not** soft: it demands
  `p_v ∈ π_u` **and** `p_u ∈ π_v`, which **no** generic point of `Y°(G)`
  satisfies (128 draws, decided exactly, zero), so nothing the induction holds
  at `G` transfers to `G + uv`. **The ear route RELOCATES the R-node
  difficulty; it does not remove it.** **(BE-43)**.
- **S-mark's pin ((BE-25)(ii)) STANDS — and the bar-lift bought one genuinely
  new fact.** The ear route needs a **third** shape, **S-dec**, marked by the
  decomposition: strictly **weaker** than S-all (finitely many pairs, named in
  advance) and not S-mark. It still meets **cross pairs** ((BE-28)(i)) whenever
  a later ear attaches at an earlier ear's interior, and avoiding that
  **requires a cycle through every degree-`≥3` vertex** — satisfied by all
  12 620 swept graphs, and **failing** at any subdivision of a non-Hamiltonian
  3-connected base, of which **Petersen** is the smallest (non-Hamiltonicity
  decided by exhaustive search). **Both gaps localise at the same place: the
  R-node.**
- **Verdict: (BE-14) OPEN and unchanged in status. HIT shape 3 (a routing

`ρ̄_{uv}`, `ρ_{uv}`, hub, `Π_v := p_v ∧ π_v`, `Z := Π_u + Π_v`, `E`, `c₂`,
`loss`, `slack`, the Klein form, the α-plane `S_p`). Added here:

- for a partition `P` of `V(G)`: `d(P)` the number of edges **not** inside a
  part, `e_in(P) = |E| − d(P)`, `value(P) = 6(|P|−1) − 5 d(P)`, and
  `f(W) = 5|E(W)| − 6(|W|−1)` the part weight of `kbare_common`'s part-sum
  identity (`f(∅) = f(singleton) = 0`);
- `Q = Q(P)`, the **quotient multigraph** on the parts of `P`, one edge per
  crossing edge of `G`; `e_Q(S)` the number of `Q`-edges with **both** ends in
  a set `S` of parts;
- a set `S` of parts is **TIGHT** when `5 e_Q(S) = 6(|S|−1)`, i.e. merging it
  leaves the value unchanged;
- `P_max`, the **coarsest optimal partition** ((BE-39)(ii));
- the **`≤L`-cycle class** of a vertex: the union-find classes generated by
  `V(C)` over all cycles `C` of `G` with `|C| ≤ L`;
- the **aggressive plane-class closure** `forced_same_plane` — seed a hub `h`
  with `A := N[h]`, repeatedly admit a hub `v` with `|N[v] ∩ A| ≥ 3` and set
  `A := A ∪ N[v]`; the forced pairs are the pairs inside one `fam(h)`. **This
  is the operator every claim below is proved or measured for**, and it
  **over**-claims forcing (it assumes every three points independent), which is
  the direction that makes an empty sweep the **stronger** statement;
- an **open ear decomposition**: a cycle `C`, then paths whose two endpoints
  are **distinct** vertices of the current graph and whose interior is new; a
  **single-edge ear** (equivalently a **chord**) is such a path of length 1.

**Carrier check, done off the landed bodies rather than the prose.** No new
Lean object is read beyond the four BINDUC read (`Graph.partitionDef`,
`Graph.deficiency`, `bodyBarDim`, `SimpleGraph.IsGeneralPositionPlacement`);
the pencil condition is read off `kbare_common.verify_pencil_witness` and
`bimage.plane_at` — *every closed star admits a common normal*, i.e. **every
closed star is coplanar** — and that reading is what (BE-43)(iii) rests on.

### Step BE38 — the two partition-lattice laws the merge inequality proves, and which the arc had not extracted

> **(BE-39)(i)** *(proven; **THE QUOTIENT SPARSITY LAW**, and `girth(Q) ≥ 6`)*
> Let `P` be optimal, `Q` its quotient. Then for **every** set `S` of parts
>
> **`5 e_Q(S) ≤ 6(|S| − 1)`.**
>
> *Proof.* Merging `S` into one part is a partition of value
> `value(P) − 6(|S|−1) + 5 e_Q(S)`, which is `≤ value(P) = f` by optimality. ∎
>
> Consequences, read off the `|S|` it is applied at:
> `|S| = 2` gives `e_Q ≤ 1`, so **`Q` is simple** — two parts of an optimal
> partition are joined by at most one edge of `G`, hence a vertex has at most
> **one** neighbour in each part other than its own. `|S| = 3, 4, 5` give
> `e_Q ≤ 2, 3, 4`, forbidding a triangle, a 4-cycle and a 5-cycle of `Q`;
> `|S| = 6` gives `e_Q ≤ 6`, so a 6-cycle is allowed and is **TIGHT**. Hence
> **`girth(Q) ≥ 6`**.
>
> Measured (`bearfull.py merge`): **EXHAUSTIVE over every connected labelled
> graph on `n = 3…6` (27 474 graphs) plus 600 seeded masks at each of
> `n = 7, 8` — 28 572 graphs, 28 633 optimal partitions and 130 331
> **ENUMERATED** subsets of their parts, `0` violations**, of which **61** are
> tight; the girth histogram is `forest: 28 572, 6: 61`, with **zero** entries
> below 6 and **zero** parallel `Q`-edges. The 61 are exactly the 6-cycles'
> finest partitions.

> **(BE-39)(ii)** *(proven; **THE JOIN LEMMA** — `δ = 0` is an equivalence
> relation)* Write `g(P) := Σ_B f(B) = value(P) − (6(n−1) − 5|E|)`, so
> `g(P) = 5 e_in(P) + 6|P| − 6n`. Then `g` is **supermodular** on the partition
> lattice:
>
> - `e_in(P ∨ P′) ≥ e_in(P) + e_in(P′) − e_in(P ∧ P′)`, because an edge inside
>   a `P`-block **or** inside a `P′`-block is inside a join block, and the
>   edges inside **both** are exactly `e_in(P ∧ P′)`;
> - `|P ∨ P′| ≥ |P| + |P′| − |P ∧ P′|`, because the bipartite
>   block-intersection graph has `|P| + |P′|` vertices, `|P ∧ P′|` edges and
>   `|P ∨ P′|` components, and `#components ≥ #vertices − #edges`.
>
> Hence `g(P ∨ P′) ≥ g(P) + g(P′) − g(P ∧ P′)`. If `P, P′` are both optimal,
> the right side is `≥ max + max − max = max`, so **`P ∨ P′` is optimal**. ∎
>
> Therefore the optimal partitions are closed under join and have a unique
> **coarsest** element `P_max`, and
>
> **`δ_uv = 0 ⟺ u` and `v` lie in one block of `P_max`.**
>
> *(⟸)* `P_max` is an optimal partition with `u, v` together, so
> `g_uv ≥ f`, and `g_uv ≤ f` always. *(⟹)* `g_uv = f` means some optimal
> partition has them together; joining it into `P_max` keeps them together. ∎
>
> **This is the tool the whole of (BE-32)(+) needed and did not have:
> *"`δ = 0`" is TRANSITIVE.** (BE-32)(ii)/(iii) prove the stronger *"no optimal
> partition separates them"*, which is transitive for a different and weaker
> reason; the join lemma makes `δ = 0` itself an equivalence relation, which is
> what lets short-cycle certificates **compose**.
>
> Measured: **61 ENUMERATED pairs** of distinct optimal partitions (only 61
> graphs under the cap have more than one optimal partition, and they are the
> 6-cycles), `0` failures; and `δ_uv = 0 ⟺` same block of `P_max` at
> **435 072** pairs, `0` failures.

### Step BE39 — the short-cycle law, which CONTAINS (BE-32)(ii) and (iii)

> **(BE-40)(i)** *(proven; **cycles of length `≤ 5` never split**)* Let `C` be
> a cycle of `G`, `P` an optimal partition, and `r` the number of edges of `C`
> whose ends lie in different parts. Going round `C`, the crossing edges form a
> **closed walk** in `Q`; by (BE-39)(i) no two `G`-edges join the same pair of
> parts, so those `r` `Q`-edges are **distinct**. A non-empty set of distinct
> edges forming a closed walk has every `Q`-vertex of **even** degree, hence
> contains a `Q`-cycle, which by (BE-39)(i) has length `≥ 6`. So
>
> **`r = 0` or `r ≥ 6`.**
>
> For `|C| ≤ 5` the second is impossible, so `r = 0`: **every cycle of length
> `≤ 5` lies inside a single part of every optimal partition.** ∎

> **(BE-40)(ii)** *(proven; the 6-cycle is the TIGHT boundary)* If `|C| = 6`
> and `r > 0` then `r = 6`, so every edge of `C` crosses; and two vertices of
> `C` in one part are impossible — adjacent-but-one puts two `G`-edges between
> the **same** pair of parts, and any other coincidence closes a `Q`-cycle of
> length `< 6`, both forbidden by (BE-39)(i). So `C` meets exactly **six**
> parts carrying **six** `Q`-edges — a **TIGHT** set, whose merge is again optimal by
> (BE-39)(i)'s equality case. Either way **some optimal partition has all of
> `C` in one block**, so by (BE-39)(ii)
>
> **`δ_xy = 0` for any `x, y` on a common cycle of length `≤ 6`**,
>
> and, `δ = 0` being an equivalence relation, for any `x, y` in one
> **`≤6`-cycle class**. ∎

> **(BE-40)(iii)** *(proven; the general bound)* With `r` crossings the walk
> visits at most `r` parts, so merging them gives
> `δ_xy ≤ 6(r−1) − 5r = r − 6 ≤ |C| − 6`:
>
> **`δ_xy ≤ max(0, L − 6)` for `x, y` on a common `L`-cycle**,
>
> which is strictly better than (BE-32)(iv)'s `δ_xy ≤ dist(x,y)` for every
> `L ≤ 11`. ∎

> **(BE-40)(iv)** *(containment, and a genuine weakening of a landed
> hypothesis)* **(BE-32)(ii)** — a common triangle — is `L = 3`.
> **(BE-32)(iii)** — `≥ 3` common neighbours — is `L = 4`, and its hypothesis
> **weakens**: two non-adjacent vertices with **`≥ 2`** common neighbours
> already lie on a 4-cycle, so `δ = 0`. Nothing is refuted; a landed theorem is
> **strengthened**, and both become instances of one statement.
>
> Measured (`bearfull.py cycles`): over the same exhaustive `n = 3…6` census
> plus 400 seeded masks at `n = 7`, **241 771 ENUMERATED `(cycle of length
> ≤ 5, optimal partition)` incidences with `0` violations**; **33 262** 6-cycle
> incidences of which **61** split into six parts forming a tight set and `0`
> violate the dichotomy; **294 500** pairs in a common `≤6`-cycle class, `0`
> with `δ ≠ 0`; **289 000** pairs with a common cycle of length `≤ 8`, `0`
> violating `δ ≤ max(0, L−6)` at the shortest one; and **61 770** non-adjacent
> pairs with `≥ 2` common neighbours — a hypothesis (BE-32)(iii) does **not**
> cover — `0` with `δ ≠ 0`.

### Step BE40 — (BE-32)(+): the closure operator named, the theorem proved at 96.2 % of instances, and the boundary located

> **(BE-41)(i)** *(proven; the **STAR-2 step**, and it contains (BE-32)(ii) and
> (iii) as its base case)* Let the aggressive closure admit a hub `v` on the
> strength of three points `x, y, z ∈ N[v] ∩ A`. Suppose two of them lie in one
> closed star `N[w]` and are **not** the degenerate pair `{v, w}`. Then `v` and
> `w` lie on a common cycle of length `3` or `4`:
>
> - `a, b ∈ N(v) ∩ N(w)` with `a, b ∉ {v, w}` give the 4-cycle
>   `v — a — w — b — v`;
> - `a = v` (so `v ∈ N[w]`, i.e. `v ∼ w`) and `b ∈ N(v) ∩ N(w)` give the
>   triangle `v — w — b — v`.
>
> By (BE-40) `δ_{vw} = 0`, and by (BE-39)(ii) these compose. **The FIRST step
> is always of this shape**: `|N[v] ∩ N[h]| ≥ 3` with `v ≁ h` means `≥ 3` common
> neighbours ((BE-32)(iii)), and with `v ∼ h` it means a common neighbour, i.e.
> a triangle ((BE-32)(ii)). So **(BE-32)(ii)/(iii) are exactly the base case of
> this induction**, and the rest of it is new. ∎
>
> Measured (`bearfull.py forced`): **401 544 forcing steps**, of which
> **401 489** are star-2 — **PROVED** — and **55** are not. Carrying only the
> star-2 links, **196 043 of 203 723** aggressively-forced pairs have `δ = 0`
> **proved with no measurement at all**; the exhaustive `n = 3…6` tier is
> **100 %** proved and every unproved pair is at `n ≥ 7`.

> **(BE-41)(ii)** *(the residue, stated exactly, and it is geometry-free)* What
> is left of (BE-32)(+) is
>
> **every aggressively-forced pair lies in one `≤6`-cycle class**,
>
> a statement about a graph and a union-find, with **no configuration, no
> genericity, no constructor and no closure-operator subtleties** in it. The
> unproved case is the **SPREAD** step: the three points come from three
> different closed stars and no two share one, so no `≤4`-cycle is available at
> `v`.
>
> Measured: **203 723** forced pairs, **`0`** outside a `≤6`-cycle class; and

> **(BE-41)(iii)** *(the boundary, LOCATED — and it is exactly where the merge

> not: `5·7 = 35 < 36 = 6·6`. So (BE-40) **cannot** be pushed past 6, and the

### Step BE41 — (b2) is a corollary of (b1), and the ear case's (β) side loses a clause

> **(BE-42)(i)** *(proven; **ONE LINE OF GRASSMANN**, and it is not a dimension
> count)* `Π_u ⊆ Z` by the definition `Z = Π_u + Π_v`. So for **any** subspace
> `X`,
>
> `dim(X ∩ Z) + dim Π_u = dim((X ∩ Z) + Π_u) + dim(X ∩ Z ∩ Π_u)
>  ≤ dim Z + dim(X ∩ Π_u)`,
>
> using `X ∩ Z ∩ Π_u = X ∩ Π_u`. With `dim Π_u = 2` and `X = ρ̄₁`:
>
> **`dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Z) ≤ dim Z − 2 + min( dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u), dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_v) )`.** ∎
>
> No genericity, no count, no transversality — a Grassmann identity and an
> inclusion. (ZJACOB (JC-6) is satisfied by construction: nothing here is
> derived *from* a dimension count.)

> **(BE-42)(ii)** *(proven; the consequence — (b2) stops being an independent
> clause)* (b2) demands
> `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Z) ≤ max(δ₁ + dim Z − 6, dim Z − 2)`. Then:
>
> - **(b1) at strength `≤ 1` gives `dim Z − 1`**, which meets (b2) exactly when
>   `δ₁ + dim Z − 6 ≥ dim Z − 1`, i.e. **`δ₁ ≥ 5`**. So **(b1) ⟹ (b2)
>   outright at `δ₁ ≥ 5`**, `dim Z` cancelling — the same cancellation
>   (BE-36) used to refute (β) as stated, now pointing the other way.
> - **(b1) sharpened to `ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u = 0` at EITHER end gives `dim Z − 2`**, i.e.
>   **(b2) at every `δ₁`**.
>
> So the three clauses of (BE-37)(ii) are **not independent**: (b2) is (b1) at
> one end, sharpened from `≤ 1` to `0`. The only pieces needing more are those
> with `min(dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u), dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_v)) ≥ 1` and `δ₁ ≤ 4`. Of those, the
> `= 2` case is `Π_u ⊆ ρ̄₁`, i.e. the **(P) trap genuinely realised**, which
> (BE-38)(iii) **asserts** does not occur below `ρ₁ = 6` (a non-vacuous
> occurrence would stop that driver); and the `= 1` case is the **series**
> shape at that end — every `u–v` path leaving `u` by the same edge, an S-node
> in the SPQR sense. There (BE-30)(i) describes `ρ̄₁` as a chain through that
> leading hinge line, (BE-38)(i) settles the **all-S** piece outright, and a
> general such piece **peels** its leading edge and recurses down the SPQR
> tree — stated here as the route, **not** as a proof. ∎

> **(BE-42)(iii)** *(the sharpening's mechanism, NAMED rather than measured)*
> Every hinge line at `u` lies in `Π_u = p_u ∧ π_u`: the closed star of `u` is
> coplanar in `π_u` ((BE-16), read off `verify_pencil_witness`), so a hinge line
> at `u` passes through `p_u` inside `π_u`. `assert_generic_star` forbids two
> hinge lines at a body from coinciding, so **any two hinge lines at `u` SPAN
> `Π_u`**. If two `u–v` paths leave `u` by different edges then `ρ̄₁` lies in

### Step BE42 — the routing verdict: the ear route is REFUTED as a replacement for the internal R-node

**The hypothesis, restated as the coordinator posed it.** Every 2-connected
graph has an **open ear decomposition** starting from a cycle — **classical**,
and the construction is Whitney's (H. Whitney, *Non-separable and planar
graphs*, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. **34** (1932), no. 2, 339–362; author, year,
title, journal, volume and pages verified against the AMS primary listing, and
**no section number is asserted**, per `CLAUDE.md` *Referencing prior work*).
(BE-18) reduces (BE-14) to 2-connected graphs; a cycle is max-degree `≤ 2`, one
of the **free** base classes ((BE-25)(iv)); and each ear **with an interior
vertex** attaches at a pair `{u,v}` that **is** a 2-cut of the enlarged graph,
so that step is exactly BEARCASE's ear case with `G₂` the ear and `G₁`
arbitrary. **Each of those four links checks out** — they were verified against
the landed statements, not against the prose that cites them. The question is
whether anything else is needed. It is.

> **(BE-43)(i)** *(proven, one line; **GAP (i) IS DECIDED**)* In a **chord-free**
> open ear decomposition the **last** ear has length `≥ 2` and no later ear
> attaches to it, so its interior vertices have degree **exactly 2** in `G`; and
> if there is no ear at all then `G` is a cycle. Hence
>
> **`G` has a chord-free open ear decomposition ⟹ `G` has a vertex of
> degree 2**,
>
> equivalently: **every graph of minimum degree `≥ 3` — in particular every
> 3-connected graph, i.e. every R-node — forces a single-edge ear in EVERY open
> ear decomposition.** ∎
>
> The counting bound `m ≤ 2n − |C| ≤ 2n − girth(G)` (each ear must add a
> vertex) is the weaker numerical shadow of the same fact; `K₄` violates it
> already (`6 > 5`).
>
> Measured (`bearfull.py eardec`): **EXHAUSTIVE over the 2-connected labelled
> graphs on `n = 3…6` (11 617) plus 900 seeded masks at each of `n = 7, 8` —
> 12 620 graphs**, per-graph **decided** by exhaustive search with two sound
> prunes: **6 968** admit a chord-free open ear decomposition, **every one** of
> them has a degree-2 vertex (`0` exceptions, which the theorem forbids), and of
> the **2 084** 3-connected graphs **ZERO** do.

> **(BE-43)(ii)** *(proven and swept; the chord step's COMBINATORIAL half is
> FREE)* Adding `uv` raises `d(P)` by one for exactly the partitions that
> separate `u` and `v`, so
>
> **`def₃(G + uv) = max( def₃(G) − δ_uv, def₃(G) − 5 )`.**
>
> *Proof.* `value_{G+uv}(P) = value_G(P) − 5·[u,v separated]`. The maximum over
> partitions with `u, v` together is `g_uv = f − δ_uv`; the maximum over the
> rest is `≤ f`, with equality whenever `δ_uv > 0`; and `f − δ_uv = g_uv ≥ 0`,
> so the `max` is never empty. ∎
>
> Measured: **EXHAUSTIVE over every connected labelled graph on `n = 3…6` and
> every non-edge — 189 587 `(graph, non-edge)` instances, `0` violations.**

> **(BE-43)(iii)** *(the obstruction, and it is not a dimension count;
> **GAP (i) is NOT soft**)* By (BE-16) the pencil condition **is** *every closed
> star coplanar*. So `G + uv` demands **`p_v ∈ π_u` AND `p_u ∈ π_v`**: the
> chord variety `Y°(G+uv)` is a **proper closed subset** of `Y°(G)`. The
> induction hands over a **generic** point of a component of `Y°(G)`, which
> therefore lies **outside** `Y°(G+uv)`. And attainment cannot be inherited by
> specialisation in any case: `dim M` is **upper** semicontinuous, so moving
> onto a proper closed subvariety can only **raise** it above the cap
> attainment demands — the semicontinuity points the **wrong way**, which is
> the same shape as the arc's other hard steps.
>
> Measured: **128** generic pencil draws from bearcase's free sampler, at
> pieces with `u, v` **non-adjacent**, each **decided exactly** (a rank
> computation over ℚ, never sampled): **`0`** satisfy both conditions. The
> codimension is **2 conditions** whenever both closed stars span a plane —
> **labelled as a count**; nothing here derives properness, smoothness or
> transversality from it.

> **(BE-43)(iv)** *(**GAP (ii)**: the third shape exists, is weaker than S-all,
> and still meets cross pairs)* The ear induction needs the welding clause at
> the **next** ear's attachment pair, so it carries a third shape — call it
> **S-dec**, marked by the **decomposition** rather than by a rooted tree.
> S-dec is strictly **weaker** than S-all (finitely many pairs, **named in
> advance**) and is not S-mark; **that weakening is the one genuinely new piece
> of information the lifted bar bought**, and it is worth recording because it
> makes the cross-pair obligation a question about a *named finite set* rather
> than about *all* pairs.
>
> It does **not** avoid cross pairs. A later ear may attach at a vertex
> **interior** to an earlier ear, and then the pair is a **cross pair** in the
> sense of (BE-28)(i) — contracting it destroys the 2-cut, so neither the
> (BE-21) `def₃` law nor the (BE-22)(i) fibre-product law reaches it. **Proved:**
> a decomposition avoiding that entirely forces **every degree-`≥3` vertex onto
> the initial cycle**, because a vertex off `C` that receives no later
> attachment has degree 2. So a **necessary** condition for the ear route to
> avoid cross pairs is that **some cycle of `G` carries every branch vertex**.
>
> Measured, and the first column is an **honest negative for this analysis**:
> **12 620 of 12 620** swept 2-connected graphs have such a cycle, so under the
> cap gap (ii) does **not** bite. It says where to look instead. For a
> **subdivision** of a base `B`, a cycle carrying every branch vertex is exactly
> a **Hamiltonian** cycle of `B`; the **Petersen** graph is 3-connected and
> **non-Hamiltonian** (decided by exhaustive search in the driver), so **every
> subdivision of Petersen** — 2-connected, not 3-connected, carrying an
> **internal R-node** — has no such cycle, and every open ear decomposition of

deliverable — **carrying shape 2's job-2 half**: (b2) is closed, as a reduction

job 1 is not closed. It is **not shape 4**: no obstruction to (BE-32)(+) was

**Job 1 ((BE-32)(+)).** **Advanced from MEASURED to PROVED at 96.2 % of
instances, and REDUCED for the rest.** The closure operator is **named** (the
aggressive one, `bimage.forced_same_plane`, which over-claims forcing). The
mechanism is a **short-cycle law** that contains both known mechanisms as its
`L = 3` and `L = 4` cases, plus a **join lemma** that makes `δ = 0` transitive
so the certificates compose. 401 489 of 401 544 forcing steps and 196 043 of
203 723 forced pairs are **proved**; the residue is the **spread** step at 55
instances, all at `n ≥ 7`; and what is left is a statement with **no geometry
in it**.

**Job 2 ((b2) for a general piece).** **CLOSED, as a reduction, and the

**Job 3 (the routing question).** **DECIDED NEGATIVE by a theorem.** Reported
as a verdict, not a preference, exactly as the spec demanded; and the negative
is worth what the spec said it was worth — it **confirms S-mark** and retires

**The price, re-quoted against BEARCASE's.**

### Caps, disclosed rather than smoothed

1. **`merge` and `cycles` are exhaustive to `n = 6` and sampled beyond.** Only
   **61** graphs under the cap have more than one optimal partition (they are
   the 6-cycles), so the **join-lemma sweep is thin** — the lemma is
   **proved**, and the sweep confirms rather than carries it. The same is true
   of the 61 tight sets.
2. **`cycles` enumerates cycles to length 8 only**, so the
   `δ ≤ max(0, L−6)` column is read at the shortest common cycle of length
   `≤ 8` and is **silent** about pairs whose only common cycles are longer.
3. **(BE-41)(ii) is MEASURED, not proved**, and is the load-bearing cap of job
   1. It reads *"no aggressively-forced pair outside a `≤6`-cycle class was
   found under this cap"*, never *"none exists"*. The `n = 7, 8, 9` tiers are
   1 400 seeded masks each; the `n = 9…13` blind hunt is seeded random and
   computes `δ` at every not-connected pair **and two further forced pairs per
   graph**, not at all of them.
4. **The direct `δ` check on forced pairs is capped at `n ≤ 7`** by the cost of
   `g_exact`; beyond that the evidence is the blind hunt's 3 802 computations.
5. **`bgrass` inherits bearcase's sampler shape guard** — branch vertices an
   independent set, each free vertex with at most one branch neighbour — so the
   battery is **subdivisions only**, and says nothing about pieces with
   adjacent branch vertices. `δ₁` is the **measured** max `dim ρ̄₁` over draws, a
   **lower** bound on the combinatorial `δ₁`, which **under**-states the (b2)
   bound — the conservative direction.
6. **(BE-42)(iii) is a mechanism, not a proof of `ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u = 0`.** The
   containment `ρ̄₁ ⊆ ⟨P⟩ ∩ ⟨Q⟩` is exact and the two `Π_u`-lines are distinct;
   concluding `0` still needs the interior lines generic against `Π_u`, and
   that is **labelled a genericity proviso**, exactly as (BE-38)(ii) was.
7. **`eardec`'s per-graph decision is exhaustive within a 400 000-state cap**
   with two sound prunes; a cap overflow is reported **UNDECIDED**, never as a
   negative (none occurred). The sweep is exhaustive to `n = 6` and 900 seeded

8. **(BE-43)(iii)'s measurement establishes only that the generic point of
   `Y°(G)` is not a chord point** — **not** that `Y°(G+uv)` is empty, nor that

9. **(BE-43)(iv)'s cross-pair necessary condition does not bite under the
   cap.** The Petersen witness is a **construction**; it shows the condition

10. **Nothing here touches the closure operator's own faithfulness.** Every
    claim is about the **aggressive** operator, which over-claims forcing; a

### Standing notation

Inherited from *Steps BE9–BE42* verbatim (`f := def₃`, `g_{uv}`, `δ_{uv}`,
`ρ̄_{uv}`, `ρ_{uv}`, hub, `Π_v := p_v ∧ π_v`, `Z := Π_u + Π_v`, `E`, `c₂`,
`loss`, `slack`, `dist_{G₁}`, the Klein form, `(b1)`/`(b2)`/`(b3)` of
(BE-37)(ii)). Added here:

- `⟨P⟩ := ⟨ℓ_e : e ∈ P⟩` for a `u–v` path `P`, the span of its hinge lines —
  the right-hand side of (BE-30)(iv); `ℓ_{P,1}` its **first** line, at `u`;
- `d_min := min_P dim⟨P⟩` over all `u–v` paths of the piece. By (BE-30)(iv),
  `δ₁ ≤ d_min` **always**; measured, `dim⟨P⟩ = min(|P|, 6)` at every path of
  every draw, so generically `d_min = min(dist_{G₁}(u,v), 6)`;
- a **series end**: `u` is one when every `u–v` path of the piece leaves `u` by
  the *same* edge `e = u w₁` — equivalently, `e` is a bridge separating `u`
  from `v`. This is a property of the **graph**, decided by connectivity (is
  there exactly one neighbour `w` of `u` that reaches `v` in `H − u`?), never
  by enumerating paths. An S-node in the SPQR sense is the special case where
  the whole piece is series;
- **path-saturated** at a configuration: `δ₁ = d_min`, i.e. `ρ̄₁` **is** the
  span of a shortest-spanning `u–v` path. Unlike a series end this is a
  property of the **configuration** — but generically of the graph, since both
  sides take their generic values;
- `ℓ_u`, `ℓ_v`: at a piece that is a series end at both ends, the two leading
  hinge lines, `ℓ_u ∈ Π_u` and `ℓ_v ∈ Π_v`.

**Carrier check, done off the landed bodies rather than the prose.** No new Lean
object is read. The pencil condition is read off
`kbare_common.verify_pencil_witness` and `bimage.plane_at` — *every closed star
admits a common normal*, i.e. **every closed star is coplanar** ((BE-16)) — and
that reading is what puts every hinge line at `u` inside `Π_u`, which is the one
geometric input (BE-44) and (BE-45) share. **No `.lean` was opened; the standing
2026-08-05 Lean hold binds.**

### Step BE43 — the reduction the spec offered: sound, decoupled, and bounded by a dimension count rather than by genericity

> **(BE-44)(i)** *(proven; **THE REDUCTION HOLDS**, and it decouples)* Let `P`,
> `Q` be `u–v` paths of the piece leaving `u` by **different** edges. By
> (BE-30)(iv), `ρ̄₁ ⊆ ⟨P⟩` and `ρ̄₁ ⊆ ⟨Q⟩`, so
>
> **`ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u ⊆ (⟨P⟩ ∩ Π_u) ∩ (⟨Q⟩ ∩ Π_u)`.**
>
> Each factor contains its own first line: `ℓ_{P,1} = p_u ∧ p_{w₁} ∈ ⟨P⟩`
> trivially, and `∈ Π_u` because `closedNbhd(u) ⊆ π_u` puts `p_{w₁}` in `π_u`
> ((BE-16)). The two first lines are distinct — `assert_generic_star` forbids
> two hinge lines at a body from coinciding — and `dim Π_u = 2`. Hence **if each
> factor is exactly its own first line, the intersection is `0`.** The
> condition is **per path**, never a joint condition on the pair: this half of
> the spec's guess is **CONFIRMED as stated**. ∎

> **(BE-44)(ii)** *(proven; **THE CORRECTION** — the condition is not a
> codimension condition on the interior lines)* `⟨P⟩ ∩ Π_u = ⟨ℓ_{P,1}⟩` is
> **equivalent to `dim⟨P⟩ ≤ 5`**, in this precise sense: `Π_u ⊆ Λ²K⁴` has
> dimension `2` in dimension `6`, so `dim⟨P⟩ = 6` gives `⟨P⟩ = Λ²K⁴` and the
> factor is **all of `Π_u`**, at **every** configuration — generic or not. So
> the reduction proves `0` only where **two** paths with distinct first edges
> each span `≤ 5`, and that is a **hard dimensional boundary**, not a
> genericity proviso to be discharged. The spec's framing — *"a codimension
> condition on the interior lines, one path at a time"* — is right about the
> shape and wrong about the difficulty: below the boundary the condition is a
> genuine open condition (discharged in (BE-46)); at or above it, it is false
> identically.
>
> Measured (`bsharp.py red`, one guarded draw at each of **37** pieces, every
> path of every piece asserted): `dim⟨P⟩ = min(|P|, 6)`;
> `dim(⟨P⟩ ∩ Π_u) = 1` **iff** `dim⟨P⟩ ≤ 5`, and then the factor **is**
> `⟨ℓ_{P,1}⟩` as a *space*; `= 2` **iff** `dim⟨P⟩ = 6`. ∎

> **(BE-44)(iii)** *(measured; the reduction is SUFFICIENT, NOT NECESSARY)* The
> reduction's bound equals the true `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u)` at **31 of 37** pieces and
> is **loose at 6**. Three of the loose rows — `K₄` subdivided ×3 at `0,1`,
> `K_{3,3}` subdivided ×3 at `0,1`, prism subdivided ×3 at `0,5` — have
> `ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u = 0` while the reduction's bound is `1` or `2`: the sharpening is
> **true beyond the reduction's reach**, because `ρ̄₁` there is far smaller than
> any single path span (`δ₁ = 0` or `3` against `d_min = 3` or `6`). The other
> three are the series pieces of (BE-45)(i), where the bound is `2` and the
> truth is `1`. So the reduction is a **tool**, not a characterization — which
> is why (BE-45), not (BE-44), is the direction's structural result. At every
> piece where the reduction *does* prove `0` (**8 of 37**) the measured value is
> `0`, **asserted rather than reported**.

### Step BE44 — the failure locus, exactly: a dichotomy of two theorems, and the landed prose it corrects

> **(BE-45)(i)** *(proven; **(M1), THE SERIES END** — no genericity, no draw)*
> Suppose every `u–v` path leaves `u` by the same edge `e = u w₁`. Then every
> `u–v` path contains `e`, so `e` is a **bridge separating `u` from `v`**: let
> `A` be the component of `H − e` containing `u` and `B` the other, so
> `v ∈ B` and `(A ∪ e) ∩ B = {w₁}`. That is a SERIES decomposition, and
> (BE-31)(i) gives
>
> `ρ̄₁ = ρ̄_{u,w₁}(A ∪ e) + ρ̄_{w₁,v}(B)`.
>
> In `A ∪ e` the vertex `w₁` is a **leaf**, so its edge multiplier is
> unconstrained and `ρ̄_{u,w₁}(A ∪ e) = K·ℓ_e` **exactly**. Since `ℓ_e` is a
> hinge line at `u` it lies in `Π_u` ((BE-16)). Hence
>
> **`⟨ℓ_e⟩ ⊆ ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u`, so `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u) ≥ 1` at EVERY configuration.** ∎
>
> This **contains** (BE-38)(i)'s path-piece row (`dim = 1`, sharp) as the special
> case where the whole piece is a path, and it is strictly more general: the
> spec's *"path pieces"* is the wrong class — a **lollipop** (a pendant path from
> `u` into a `θ`, whose far hub is `v`) is a series end with **three** `u–v`
> paths and `δ₁ ≠ d_min`, and the sharpening fails there too.

> **(BE-45)(ii)** *(proven; **(M2), PATH SATURATION** — and it needs no
> hypothesis on the first edges at all)* Suppose `δ₁ = d_min`, and let `P`
> realize the minimum. By (BE-30)(iv) `ρ̄₁ ⊆ ⟨P⟩`, and the dimensions agree, so
> **`ρ̄₁ = ⟨P⟩` as SPACES**. Hence
>
> **`ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u = ⟨P⟩ ∩ Π_u ⊇ ⟨ℓ_{P,1}⟩ ≠ 0`, at both ends.** ∎
>
> Asserted as `same_space(ρ̄₁, ⟨P⟩)` at every firing row, never as an equality of
> dimensions. Note `δ₁ = 6` is the sub-case `d_min = 6`: (M2) **subsumes the
> vacuous corner**, where the intersection is all of `Π_u`.

> **(BE-45)(iii)** *(the consequence for the arc — **A LANDED PROSE SENTENCE IS
> CORRECTED**, and its own numbers already said so)* (BE-38)(iii) reported
> `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u)` as `0` at 12 pieces, `1` at 7 and `2` at 5, and summarised:
> *"the intersection is `1` for path-like sides, `0` wherever two `u–v` paths
> leave `u` by different edges, and never `2` below `ρ₁ = 6`."* The **first and
> third clauses stand**. The **second is false**: `K₄` subdivided ×5 at `0,1` and
> at `0,2`, `K_{3,3}` subdivided ×5 at `0,3`, prism subdivided ×5 at `0,1`,
> `θ(5,6,7)`, `θ(5,7,9)` all have **three** distinct first edges at `u` and
> `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u) = 1`, by (M2) with `δ₁ = d_min = 5`. These are exactly the rows
> BEARFULL's `bgrass` recorded as *"every piece with `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u) = 1` came out
> at `δ₁ = 5`"* — **the two measurements agree; only the prose was wrong**, and
> (BE-42)(iii) inherited it when it named its mechanism *"the reason behind
> (BE-38)(iii)'s measured `0` wherever …"*. The mechanism is real (it is
> (BE-44)(i)); what it does not have is **sufficiency**. **This is a
> candidate-side prose correction, not a refutation of any landed measurement**
> — the same shape as (BE-36), and it is the second time in this sub-arc that a
> summary sentence outran its own table.

> **(BE-45)(iv)** *(the CONVERSE, and its status is deliberately weaker)*
> **Where neither mechanism fires, the sharpening holds** — `0` mismatches over
> **49** pieces (37 inside bearcase's guard, 12 outside it) at up to 8
> independent draws each. Of the **11** such pieces, **8** are **PROVED** by
> (BE-44)(i) together with (BE-46)'s openness step; **3** are **MEASURED ONLY**

### Step BE45 — the genericity proviso, discharged: openness, irreducibility, and why one witness is a proof

> **(BE-46)(i)** *(proven; **THE OPENNESS STEP**)* Fix the shape and let `U` be
> the locus of configurations at which `dim ρ̄₁` attains its generic value. On
> `U` the row space of the defining matrix has constant rank, so
> `config ↦ (ρ̄₁, Π_u)` is a **morphism** `U → Gr(δ₁,6) × Gr(2,6)`; the incidence
> locus `{(A,B) : dim(A ∩ B) ≥ 1}` is **closed** in that product (it is a
> determinantal condition on `A + B`). Hence `{dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u) ≥ 1} ∩ U` is closed
> in `U` and **`{ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u = 0}` is open in `U`**. ∎
>
> The restriction to `U` is not cosmetic: (BE-37)(i)'s own recorded caveat is
> that a difference of lower-semicontinuous functions is not upper
> semicontinuous once `dim ρ̄₁` drops, and `U` is exactly where that objection
> does not apply. This is the same hypothesis (β) is posed under.

> **(BE-46)(ii)** *(proven; **IRREDUCIBILITY, AND WHY ONE WITNESS SUFFICES**)*
> The free parametrization of (BE-38)(iii) — a (point, plane) flag at each
> branch vertex and at `u`, `v`, then a free point in a plane at each remaining
> vertex — is a **product** of flag data with affine planes, hence
> **irreducible**; so is (BE-48)'s extension (its extra vertices range over meet
> **lines** and its constrained points are **rational functions** of the plane
> data, both of which preserve irreducibility). On an irreducible variety a
> non-empty open set is **dense**, and finitely many non-empty opens meet —
> which is (BE-25)(i)'s simultaneity argument, reused verbatim rather than
> re-derived. Therefore:
>
> **one exhibited exact-ℚ configuration with `ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u = 0` PROVES the
> sharpening on a dense open subset of that shape's stratum.**
>
> And by (BE-37)(i)(3) the (β) side is **existential** — one configuration per
> piece settles it — so a dense open is not merely evidence, it is *more than
> the statement needs*. **The genericity proviso (BE-42)(iii) disclosed is
> DISCHARGED in this precise sense.** ∎

> **(BE-46)(iii)** *(the witnesses, and the F27 asymmetry stated in both
> directions)* `bsharp.py gen`: **37 pieces × 8 independent seeded draws =
> 296** guarded configurations, exact ℚ, each through `assert_generic_star`
> **and** `verify_pencil_witness`, with the chosen flag at `u` and at `v`
> **asserted** equal to `plane_at`'s closed-star flag. **11 pieces exhibit
> `ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u = 0`** — each a proof, per (ii). **26 pieces reach `1` or `2` at
> every one of their 8 draws**; by F27 a single nonzero draw would be an
> upper-bound artefact, so the count is stated — but for these pieces the
> evidence is not what carries the claim: **(BE-45)'s identities are**, and the
> draws only confirm them. `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u)` **varied over the attaining draws at
> 0 pieces**, so the reported value is the generic one wherever the shape has a
> generic value at all.

> **(BE-46)(iv)** *(what is NOT discharged, said plainly)* The class-level
> statement over all pieces. (i)+(ii) turn *one shape's* sharpening into a
> theorem from one witness; they do not produce the witness, and nothing here
> bounds the shapes needing one. That is the same wall (BE-37)(i) records at
> the end of its own consequences, and this direction does not move it.

### Step BE47 — job 3: the adjacent-branch-vertex parametrization, which is where the residual window lives

> **(BE-48)(i)** *(constructed; **THE FIRST PARAMETRIZATION PAST bearcase's
> SHAPE GUARD**)* bearcase's free sampler requires the branch vertices to be an
> **independent set** and every free vertex to have **at most one** branch
> neighbour — which is why every landed battery in this sub-arc is
> *subdivisions with `r ≥ 3`*, and why (BE-38)(iii) disclosed that it *"says
> nothing about pieces with adjacent branch vertices"*. The extension: choose
> the plane `π_z` at **every** branch vertex first, then place points against
> the planes.
>
> - a branch vertex with **no** branch neighbour: free in `π_z` (2 parameters);
> - with **one**: forced onto the **meet line** `π_z ∩ π_{z'}` (1 parameter),
>   because the pencil condition at `z'` demands `p_z ∈ π_{z'}` and vice versa;
> - with **two**: forced to the **triple-plane point** `π_z ∩ π_{z'} ∩ π_{z''}`
>   (0 parameters, unique generically);
> - a free vertex with two branch neighbours: forced onto their meet line.
>
> Supported: branch subgraph of maximum degree `≤ 2`, free vertices with `≤ 2`
> branch neighbours. **Every draw still passes `assert_generic_star` AND
> `verify_pencil_witness`**, which is what makes the construction self-checking
> rather than self-certifying: an error in the algebra shows up as a rejected
> draw, not as a wrong figure.

> **(BE-48)(ii)** *(the sampler RE-DERIVES a landed confinement law rather than
> assuming it)* A **triangle** on two adjacent branch vertices `z, z'` puts the
> third vertex's point on `π_z ∩ π_{z'}` as well, so `p_z, p_{z'}, p_x` are
> collinear and the two hinge lines at `z` **coincide** — the gate rejects.
> That is exactly **(BE-30)(iii)(c)**, BZAVOID's triangle propagation, arriving
> here as a *limit of the parametrization* instead of a hypothesis. It is the
> reason the adjacent-branch battery is triangle-free by construction.

### Verdict, classification, and the price

- **HIT shape 2, with a refutation attached.** The direction's question is
  **closed**: `ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u = 0` is **proved** where it is true (the openness +
  irreducibility argument plus an exhibited witness, per shape), **refuted**
  where it is not (two independent identities), and the boundary between them
  is **exact** — a dichotomy with `0` mismatches over 49 pieces. The
  **genericity proviso (BE-42)(iii) disclosed is discharged**; the reduction the
  spec offered is **sound, and its limit is a dimension count**.
- **The ear case's (β) side.** (b1)+(b2) are discharged at **every** piece
  outside one named window, by four routes that were already landed
  ((BE-38)(ii), (BE-42)(ii) branch 1, the vacuous corner, and the sharpening
  itself where available). The window — **series at both ends, `δ₁ ≤ 4`,
  `dist ≥ 5`** — has a **named checkable substitute**, `ρ̄₁ ∩ Z = ⟨ℓ_u, ℓ_v⟩`,
  exhibited at 5 of 5 window pieces. **So (β) is at (b3) plus that window**, not
  at (b3) alone: the prep's expected outcome is *narrowed but not reached*, and
  saying so is the point.
- **The price, stated as a price.** The window's substitute is **exhibited per
  piece**, not proved as a class statement; (BE-45)'s converse is proved at 8 of
  11 pieces and measured at 3; (BE-46)'s witnesses are per shape. Nothing here
  is a uniform statement over pieces — which is the same wall the whole sub-arc
  reports, and this direction neither moves it nor pretends to.
- **Untouched.** `PencilPair K 3 G`, `hbareSplit`, (BE-14)-for-all-`G`, the
  2-cut composition lemma, S-mark, (BE-32)(+), the short-cycle law, and the
  refuted ear-decomposition route (**(BE-43)**, still refuted). **Not a PENCIL
  event.**

### Verification

Every claim above is reproduced by
`python3 notes/scripts/w4/bsharp.py {red|split|gen|hyp|adj|validate}`, run from
the repo root; `validate` runs all five modes at a reduced tier in ~280 s. The
verification bar is off the **shipped** driver, and the following are the
load-bearing asserts (a failure stops the run, it is not reported):

1. **Every draw is a pencil configuration.** `assert_generic_star` **and**
   `kbare_common.verify_pencil_witness` on **every** draw of **every** mode —
   497 guarded draws in total across the five modes. The (BE-44)/(BE-45)
   arguments *consume* the first of those (no two hinge lines at a body
   coincide), so a draw that skipped it would test nothing.
2. **The flags are the closed-star flags.** At `u` and at `v`, the chosen plane
   is `assert`ed equal to `bimage.plane_at`'s closed-star plane whenever the
   closed star determines one, and `Π_u`, `Π_v` are `assert`ed 2-dimensional
   and `assert`ed **inside `Z` as identities of spaces**.
3. **Every subspace claim is an identity of SPACES.** `same_space` /
   `contains`, never an equality of dimensions: `ℓ_{P,1} ∈ ⟨P⟩` and `∈ Π_u`;
   the reduction's right-hand side contains `ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u` ((BE-30)(iv), re-checked
   per draw); `ρ̄₁ = ⟨P⟩` at every (M2) row; `⟨ℓ_e⟩ ⊆ ρ̄₁` at every (M1) row;
   `⟨ℓ_u, ℓ_v⟩ ⊆ ρ̄₁ ∩ Z` and the window identity at every window row.
4. **The per-path invariant is asserted, not reported** — `dim⟨P⟩ = min(|P|,6)`,
   `dim(⟨P⟩ ∩ Π_u) = 1 ⟺ dim⟨P⟩ ≤ 5 ⟺` the factor is `⟨ℓ_{P,1}⟩` — at every
   path of every piece in `red`.
5. **The dichotomy is asserted.** `split` and `adj` both `assert` that a
   mechanism fires **iff** the measured `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u) ≥ 1`; a mismatch stops
   the run. `hyp` `assert`s that no piece is unclassified and that the window
   identity holds inside the window.
6. **Exact ℚ throughout**, every rng seeded from a printed literal
   (`20260828`), zero floating point.

### Caps, disclosed rather than smoothed

1. **The converse of the dichotomy is not a theorem.** *"Neither mechanism
   fires ⟹ `ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u = 0`"* is proved at **8 of 11** applicable pieces (via
   (BE-44)(i) + (BE-46)) and **measured at 3**. A piece where neither fires and
   the sharpening still failed would be the interesting object, and the battery
   does not contain one.
2. **(BE-46) is per shape, not per class.** One witness proves one shape's
   stratum. Nothing here bounds how many shapes need witnesses, and the
   irreducibility step is asserted for **these two parametrizations**, not for
   an arbitrary piece's pencil stratum.
3. **`δ₁` is the MEASURED maximum over draws**, a lower bound on the generic
   `δ₁` — which under-states the (b2) bound, the conservative direction, and
   which for (M2) is the **safe** direction too (exhibiting `δ₁ = d_min` at one
   draw proves the generic value is `d_min`, since `δ₁ ≤ d_min` always).
4. **The new sampler's own guard.** Branch subgraph of maximum degree `≤ 2`,
   free vertices with `≤ 2` branch neighbours. A branch vertex with **three**
   branch neighbours is rejected — its point would be over-determined by four
   planes — so unsubdivided `K₄` and denser cores remain out of reach. That is a
   **smaller** gap than bearcase's, not none.
5. **Path enumeration is capped at 4000** simple `u–v` paths per piece; the cap
   was **not** hit at any battery piece (reported per run).
6. **The battery is 49 pieces, not a sweep.** `d_min ≤ 6` and `δ₁ ≤ 6` make the
   arithmetic small, but the *shapes* are hand-chosen — subdivisions of `K₄`,
   `K_{3,3}`, the prism, thetas, cycles, paths, lollipops, barbells, chorded
   thetas. No claim here is a statement about all pieces.
7. **`dim Z = 4` in (BE-47)(iii).** The window identity is derived at
   `dim Z = 4` (the generic flag regime); at `dim Z = 3` (`π_u = π_v`) the (b2)
   bound is `1` while `⟨ℓ_u, ℓ_v⟩` still has dimension `2`, so **(b2) would fail
   outright** — but that regime is (BE-37)(iii)'s `π_u = π_v` residue, where
   (BE-32)(ii)/(iii)/(+) give `δ_{uv} = 0` and the composition is not at issue.
   Flagged rather than folded in.

**What tests the SHAPE — stated first, because (b3) is not a dimension bound.**
Unlike (b1) and (b2), (b3) asks whether a subspace *is of a given form*, and
under **ZJACOB (JC-6)** no dimension count may stand in for that. The test used
throughout, and the one every mode runs, is:

> a 2-dimensional `A ⊆ Λ²K⁴` is a **pencil** iff the Klein form vanishes
> **identically** on it — three exact-ℚ scalars `⟨a,a⟩`, `⟨a,b⟩`, `⟨b,b⟩` on a
> basis — and a pencil has a **vertex**, the common point of its lines. Inside
> `E = Π_u + Π_v = M ∧ L` the pencils are exactly the two **rulings** of a
> quadric surface, and the vertex separates them: **vertex on `M` ⟹ `y ∧ L`,
> the opposite ruling ((b3) fails); vertex on `L` ⟹ `M ∧ z`, the ear's own
> image at `m = 1`.**

Every count that appears below is labelled a **count** ((BE-27)); none of them
is offered as a settlement of (b3).

**Status, stated before the mathematics.**

- **(b3) IS THE CHEAPEST CLAUSE, and a SEPARATION THEOREM is why.** `Π_u` and
  `Π_v` are themselves members of the `y ∧ L` ruling (`Π_u = p_u ∧ L`,
  `Π_v = p_v ∧ L`), and **distinct members of one ruling of a quadric surface
  meet in `0`**. So if `ρ̄₁ ∩ E` *were* a `y ∧ L`, then at `y ∈ {p_u, p_v}` it
  would put a whole pencil inside `ρ̄₁` and **refute (b1)**, and at any other
  `y` it would force `ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u = ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_v = 0` — **the sharpening, at both
  ends**. By (BE-45) the sharpening **fails** whenever (M1) a series end or
  (M2) path saturation fires. Hence **(b3) holds at every configuration where
  either mechanism fires at either end**, and in particular **throughout
  (BE-47)(ii)'s residual window**, which is (M1) at both ends. **The (β) side's
  two open obligations are DISJOINT: no piece can carry both.** **(BE-50)**.
- **THE HONEST DOMAIN IS NARROWER THAN THE CLAUSE SUGGESTS, and outside it (b3)
  is STRUCK rather than proved.** (b3) is posed only where `E = M ∧ L` is
  4-dimensional and the quadric surface is smooth: `π_u ≠ π_v` **and** the flags
  **cross-incidence-free** (`p_u ∉ π_v`, `p_v ∉ π_u`). At `uv ∈ E(G₁)` the
  pencil condition **forces** cross-incidence, `dist_{G₁}(u,v) = 1`, and

  `A ⊆ Λ²π` meets **every** image pencil, because two pencils of one plane

path-saturated, `ℓ_u`/`ℓ_v`, and `(b1)`/`(b2)`/`(b3)` of (BE-37)(ii)). Added
here:

- the **opposite ruling** `R_M := {y ∧ L : y ∈ M}` and the **image ruling**
  `R_L := {M ∧ z : z ∈ L}`, the two families of totally singular 2-spaces

  separately because this direction separates them.

### Step BE48 — the honest domain of (b3), and the three regimes in which it is struck rather than proved

> **(BE-49)(i)** *(proven; **THE RULING GEOMETRY**, and it is elementary)*
> Suppose `π_u ≠ π_v` and the flags are cross-incidence-free. Then `p_u ∉ L`,
> so `π_u = p_u ∨ L` and
>
> **`Π_u = p_u ∧ π_u = p_u ∧ L`, and likewise `Π_v = p_v ∧ L`;**
>
> hence `E = Π_u + Π_v = M ∧ L`, which is 4-dimensional because `M` and `L` are
> **skew** (`M ⊆ π_u` would need `p_v ∈ π_u`). The decomposable elements of `E`
> form a smooth quadric surface `P(M) × P(L)`, whose two rulings are `R_M` and
> `R_L`. **`Π_u` and `Π_v` are members of `R_M`** — the ruling (BE-33)(R) calls
> *opposite* — and the ear's image at `m = 1` is `ρ̄₂ = M ∧ p_1` with
> `p_1 ∈ π_u ∩ π_v = L`, a member of `R_L`. Distinct members of one ruling meet
> in `0`; members of opposite rulings meet in a **point**. ∎
>
> Asserted at **12** drawn flag triples as identities of spaces (`Π_u = p_u ∧ L`
> and `Π_v = p_v ∧ L` by `same_space`, `E = M ∧ L`, `M`/`L` skew), together with
> all `5 × 5` same-ruling and `5 × 4` opposite-ruling incidences per draw and
> the vertex-based shape test on every one; the verdict `other` — a pencil in
> `E` whose vertex lies on neither line — **never occurs**, and would `assert`.

> **(BE-49)(ii)** *(proven; **`uv ∈ E(G₁)`: (b3) IS FREE**)* Then
> `dist_{G₁}(u,v) = 1`, so (BE-30)(iv) gives `δ₁ ≤ 1` and `ρ̄₁` **cannot
> contain** a 2-dimensional pencil. This is a **count** ((BE-27)) — and a
> *containment* impossibility rather than a genericity or transversality count,
> so it does not offend **JC-6**: nothing here derives properness from a
> codimension. Asserted at both adjacent battery rows (measured `δ₁ = 0`).
> Note the flags there are cross-incident by force, so the ruling picture is
> degenerate anyway (`dim E = 3`, `Π_u ∩ Π_v = ⟨p_u ∧ p_v⟩`, asserted at 12
> draws).

> **(BE-49)(iii)** *(proven; **`π_u = π_v`: (b3) IS ILL-POSED, AND MUST BE
> STRUCK**)* There `L = π_u ∩ π_v` is not a line and `y ∧ L` is not a term, so
> (b3) as written has no meaning. It is also **unnecessary**: `E = Λ²π` is
> 3-dimensional, **every** 2-dimensional subspace of it is a pencil `y ∧ π`
> with `y ∈ π`, and any two pencils of one plane share the line joining their
> vertices — so `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ ρ̄₂) ≥ 1` for **every** 2-dimensional `ρ̄₁ ∩ Z`,
> **irrespective of shape**. That is precisely `lossZ = 2 + c₂ − 3 = 1` with
> `c₂ = 2`. **The mechanism is (Z), not a separate (R)**, and the repair to
> (BE-37)(ii) is to **delete (b3) from the hypothesis in this regime**, not to
> prove it. ∎ Asserted at **278** `(A, ρ̄₂)` pairs over 12 equal-plane flag
> draws, every one meeting.

> **(BE-49)(iv)** *(the fourth regime, which (BE-37)(ii) never states)*
> Cross-incidence at a **non-adjacent** pair is a codimension-1 accident of the
> **configuration**: `M` then meets `L`, `E` is no longer `M ∧ L`, the quadric
> surface degenerates and (BE-33)(R)'s derivation does not run. It is **not**
> excluded by `uv ∉ E(G₁)` and **not** excluded by `assert_generic_star`. Since
> (β) is **existential** over configurations ((BE-37)(i)(3)), a draw at which it
> happens is simply not the draw the statement is evaluated at — but it is a
> side-condition the reduction's prose omits, and it is **counted, never
> smoothed**: **3** of 395 hunt draws, `0` of 196 witness draws, `0` of 49
> `sep` rows.

**So (b3)'s honest domain is: `π_u ≠ π_v`, flags cross-incidence-free, `m = 1`.**
Everywhere else the clause is free, ill-posed, or not posed at all.

### Step BE49 — the separation theorem: a (b3) failure forces the sharpening at both ends

> **(BE-50)(i)** *(proven; **(b1) ALREADY DISCHARGES (b3) AT THE TWO
> DISTINGUISHED POINTS**)* If `ρ̄₁ ∩ E = y ∧ L` with `y = p_u`, then
> `Π_u = p_u ∧ L ⊆ ρ̄₁`, so `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u) = 2` and **(b1) fails**. Likewise at
> `y = p_v`. ∎
>
> This is the **converse** of (BE-33)(ii)'s own remark that *"(P) is the special
> case of (R) at the two distinguished points of `M`"*: read forward it says (P)
> is contained in (R); read backward it says the part of (R) that (P) covers is
> already excluded by (b1). What (b3) must actually rule out is therefore only
> `y ∉ {p_u, p_v}`.

> **(BE-50)(ii)** *(proven; **THE SEPARATION**, and it is one line of incidence
> geometry)* Suppose `ρ̄₁ ∩ E = y ∧ L` with `y ∈ M ∖ {p_u, p_v}`. By
> (BE-49)(i), `y ∧ L` and `Π_u` are **distinct members of the same ruling
> `R_M`**, so `(y ∧ L) ∩ Π_u = 0`. Since `Π_u ⊆ E`,
>
> **`ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u = (ρ̄₁ ∩ E) ∩ Π_u = (y ∧ L) ∩ Π_u = 0`, and the same at `v`.** ∎
>
> *(The disjointness, without invoking the surface: a common nonzero element
> would be a decomposable `p_u ∧ x = y ∧ x'` with `x, x' ∈ L`, forcing
> `p_u ∈ y ∨ L`; but `y ∈ M` and `p_u ∈ M` with `p_u ≠ y` then put `M` inside
> the plane `y ∨ L`, so `M` and `L` would meet — contradicting skewness.)*

> **(BE-50)(iii)** *(proven; **THE COMPLEMENTARITY** — the direction's
> structural result)* Combining (i), (ii) with **(BE-45)**: the sharpening
> `ρ̄₁ ∩ Π_u = 0` **fails** at `u` whenever (M1) `u` is a series end or (M2) the
> configuration is path-saturated, and by (BE-45)(ii) (M2) fails the sharpening
> at **both** ends at once. Therefore
>
> **(M1) at `u`, or (M1) at `v`, or (M2) ⟹ (b3) holds.**
>
> In particular **(b3) holds throughout (BE-47)(ii)'s residual window**, which is
> (M1) at **both** ends. ∎
>
> **The consequence for the ear case.** (β)'s two remaining obligations —
> BSHARP's window identity `ρ̄₁ ∩ Z = ⟨ℓ_u, ℓ_v⟩` and (b3) — are **disjoint**:
> every piece where the window is at issue has (b3) for free, and every piece
> where (b3) could conceivably fail has (b1)+(b2) discharged by the sharpening
> ((BE-42)(ii), (BE-46)). This is the opposite of the arc's usual shape, where
> residues pile up at the same object; here the case split that made (b1)/(b2)
> hard is exactly what makes (b3) easy.

> **(BE-50)(iv)** *(what the battery does and does not certify here, said
> plainly)* `brule.py sep` **asserts** (i)–(iii) per row rather than reporting
> them — but with `0` failures the assertion is a **guard**, and it never fired.
> **What carries (BE-50) is the proof, not the battery.** What the battery does
> carry non-vacuously is the **contrapositive guard**, asserted at the **33** of
> 49 rows where a mechanism fires: `ρ̄₁` meets `Π_u` or `Π_v` there, which

### Step BE50 — the (R)/(Z) dominance, and the inference inside (BE-37)(ii) that it corrects

> **(BE-51)(i)** *(proven; **(Z) DOMINATES (R) OFF THE EQUALITY REGIME**)* Let
> `W := ρ̄₁ ∩ E` with `dim W = 3`, on the honest domain, at `m = 1`. `P(W)` is a
> **plane** of `P(E) ≅ P³`, and a plane meets the quadric surface in a **conic**
> — smooth, or a pair of lines one from each ruling. Either way `W` carries **at
> most one** member of `R_M` and **at most one** of `R_L`. Hence
> `dim(W ∩ M ∧ z) = 1` for all but at most one `z ∈ L`, so the minimum over the
> ear's own modulus is `lossR = 1`; and `lossZ = dim W + c₂ − dim Z = 3+2−4 = 1`
> as well. At `dim W = 4`, `E ⊆ ρ̄₁` contains `ρ̄₂` outright and
> `lossP = lossZ = 2`. **So `lossR ≤ lossZ` whenever `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ E) ≥ 3`.** ∎

> **(BE-51)(ii)** *(**A LANDED INFERENCE IS CORRECTED**; the conclusion is not)*
> (BE-37)(ii) states *"Suppose (b1) … (b2) … (b3) … **Then `lossP = lossR = 0`**"*.
> The `lossR = 0` half is **false as an inference**: (b3) is an **equality**
> test, so it is silent about `ρ̄₁ ⊇ y ∧ L` once `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ E) ≥ 3` — which
> (b2) permits at `δ₁ ≥ 5`. The correct statement is (i)'s `lossR ≤ lossZ`, and
> since the reduction bounds `loss` by `max(lossP, lossZ, lossR)` anyway, **the
> conclusion `loss ≤ slack`, the enumeration over 91 arithmetic cases, and the
> 4-row residue are all unchanged.** This is a **prose/inference correction with

> (BE-45)(iii) — and it is recorded here **and at (BE-37)(ii) itself**, per F12.
>

> literally stated is the RIGHT hypothesis.** The stronger containment form

### Step BE51 — one witness per shape: openness, properness, irreducibility

> **(BE-52)(i)** *(proven; **THE BAD LOCUS IS CLOSED**, and properness is the
> step (BE-46) did not need)* Fix the shape and let `U` be the locus where
> `dim ρ̄₁` attains its generic value and the flags are cross-incidence-free. On
> `U`, `config ↦ ρ̄₁` is a **morphism** to `Gr(δ₁,6)` (constant rank), and
> `config ↦ (M, L)` is a morphism of the flag data. Consider
>
> **`I := {(config, y) ∈ U × P(M) : y ∧ L ⊆ ρ̄₁}`.**
>
> `I` is **closed** in the projectivized bundle `P(M) → U` — it is the
> vanishing of the `2 × 2` minors of the matrix
> `[⟨n, p_u ∧ l⟩, ⟨n, p_v ∧ l⟩]_{n, l}` in the coordinates of `y`, a
> determinantal condition, which is literally the rank test `ruling_vertex`
> runs. `P(M) → U` is a **`P¹`-bundle**, hence **proper** over `U`, so the
> projection `I → U` is a **closed map**, and the (b3)-bad locus is closed in
> `U` — that is,
>
> **`{ρ̄₁ contains no opposite-ruling pencil}` is OPEN in `U`.** ∎
>
> The properness step is genuinely extra: (BE-46) tested a **fixed** pair
> `(ρ̄₁, Π_u)`, whereas (b3) quantifies over a **family** `y ∈ M`, and an image
> of a closed set is not closed without it.

> **(BE-52)(ii)** *(proven; **ONE WITNESS SUFFICES**, reusing (BE-46)(ii)
> verbatim)* Both free parametrizations — (BE-38)(iii)'s and (BE-48)(i)'s — are
> **irreducible**, so a non-empty open subset is **dense** and finitely many
> meet ((BE-25)(i)). With (i), **one exhibited exact-ℚ configuration at which
> `ρ̄₁` contains no `y ∧ L` proves (b3) on a dense open subset of that shape's
> stratum** — and by (BE-37)(i)(3) the (β) side is **existential**, so a dense
> open is more than the statement needs. ∎

> Note the argument is run on the **containment** form, which is the closed one;
> by (BE-51)(ii) that is the stronger condition, so it implies (b3) as stated.

> **(BE-52)(iii)** *(the witnesses, and the F27 asymmetry in the direction it

- **The ear case's (β) side.** With BSHARP's (b1)/(b2) result, **(β) is at the

### Verification

Every claim above is reproduced by
`python3 notes/scripts/w4/brule.py {dom|sep|domin|wit|hunt|validate}`, run from
the repo root; `validate` runs all five modes at a reduced tier in ~330 s (measured 326–340 s over three runs). The
verification bar is off the **shipped** driver, and the following are the
load-bearing asserts (a failure stops the run, it is not reported):

1. **Every piece draw is a pencil configuration.** `assert_generic_star`
   **and** `kbare_common.verify_pencil_witness` on **every** draw of **every**
   mode — **637** guarded piece configurations across `sep`, `wit` and `hunt`,
   plus the flag draws of `dom` and `domin`. The chosen flags at `u` and `v`
   are `assert`ed equal to `bimage.plane_at`'s closed-star flags.
2. **The ruling geometry is an identity of SPACES, not of dimensions.**
   `same_space` / `contains` throughout: `Π_u = p_u ∧ L`, `Π_v = p_v ∧ L`,
   `E = M ∧ L`, `M`/`L` skew (`rank = 4`), `Π_u ∩ Π_v = ⟨p_u ∧ p_v⟩` in the
   cross-incident regime, and `E = Λ²π` at equal planes.
3. **The shape test is a KLEIN-FORM test, never a dimension test.** A
   2-dimensional `A` is called a pencil only when `⟨x,y⟩ = 0` for **every**
   pair from a basis; the ruling is then decided by the **vertex**
   (`rank[p_u, p_v, y] = 2` versus `rank[L, y] = 2`). The verdict `other` — a
   pencil in `E` whose vertex is on neither — is `assert`ed impossible.
4. **The containment form is CAP-FREE in `y`.** `ruling_vertex` decides
   *"`ρ̄₁ ⊇ y ∧ L` for some `y ∈ M`"* by one exact `rank ≤ 1` test on a
   2-column matrix over the whole 1-parameter family — **no sampling of `y`
   anywhere** — and the equality form is `assert`ed to imply it at every row.
5. **The separation theorem is asserted per row** (a guard: with `0` failures it
   never fires), and its **contrapositive** is asserted non-vacuously at the 33
   rows where a mechanism fires.
6. **The (R)/(Z) dominance is checked against the LANDED predicate**, not
   against itself: `bimage.bad_predicate` versus `bimage.reach_measured` at
   built 3- and 4-dimensional `W ⊆ E` containing a `y ∧ L`, 8/8 and 8/8.
7. **Exact ℚ throughout**, every rng seeded from a printed literal
   (`20260828`), zero floating point.

### Caps, disclosed rather than smoothed

1. **The battery is 49 hand-chosen pieces, not a sweep** — bsharp's, inherited
   whole (subdivisions of `K₄` / `K_{3,3}` / the prism, thetas, cycles, paths,
   lollipops, barbells, chorded thetas). No claim here is a statement about all
   pieces.
2. **(BE-48)(i)'s sampler cap, inherited and disclosed as required.** Branch
   subgraph of maximum degree `≤ 2`, free vertices with `≤ 2` branch
   neighbours; a branch vertex with **three** branch neighbours is rejected, so
   unsubdivided `K₄` and denser cores are still out of reach for the 12 pieces
   that use it. bearcase's own guard (branch vertices an independent set)
   applies to the other 37.
3. **`δ₁` is the measured value at one draw** — a lower bound on the generic
   `δ₁` — which under-states `dim(ρ̄₁ ∩ E)` and therefore **under**-reports
   candidate (b3) failures. That is the *unsafe* direction for a hunt, and it is
   why the hunt runs 8 independent seeds per piece rather than one; `0` pieces
   varied their verdict across draws.
4. **The no-mechanism class is where the residue lives, and it is small here.**
   Of 392 hunt draws, 111 sit at a piece where neither (M1) nor (M2) fires —
   that is the only class (BE-50) leaves open, and (BE-45)(iv) already records
   that 3 of its 11 pieces rest on a draw rather than a proof.
5. **Cross-incidence is a configuration side-condition the reduction omits**,
   and this direction only *names* it; it does not characterize which graphs
   make it unavoidable at a non-adjacent pair (none in the battery: 3 of 395
   draws, all recoverable by reseeding).
6. **`dim Z = 4` throughout the honest domain.** The `dim Z = 3` regime is
   handled by (BE-49)(iii) and (BE-53)(iv), not by measurement — no equal-plane
   piece is drawn, because the samplers do not produce one.
7. **Path enumeration is capped at 4000** simple `u–v` paths per piece
   (inherited from `bsharp`); the cap was **not** hit at any battery row.
8. **(BE-51)(iii) is a check, not a re-run.** It builds `W` by hand; it does
   **not** re-run `bimage.py badA` or `hunt`, whose figures are cited. Its
   *"at most one member of each ruling"* assertion is a **sampled guard** at 8
   parameter values in each ruling — what carries that claim is (BE-51)(i)'s
   conic argument, not the sample.
